claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

✅ **Alex meets all the key requirements:**
- **Age**: At 19, Alex is under the age 20 threshold
- **Education**: Alex is in approved education, which allows Child Benefit to continue beyond age 16
- **Living arrangement**: Alex lives with you, which establishes your responsibility for them
- **Work status**: Alex doesn't work 24+ hours per week (which would disqualify them if they left education)
- **No disqualifying factors**: Alex hasn't started an apprenticeship, isn't receiving benefits in their own right, and isn't in care or hospital

**What you should know:**
- Child Benefit can continue until Alex turns 20, as long as they remain in approved education or training
- If Alex's circumstances change (e.g., leaves education, starts working 24+ hours/week, or starts receiving certain benefits), you must inform HMRC as this could affect your entitlement
- If you or your partner earn over £60,000 individually, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge

You can proceed with your Child Benefit claim or continue receiving it if you're already claiming!

reasonings:
Alex meets all the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit:

1. Age requirement: Alex is 19 years old, which is under the age 20 threshold.

2. Education/training requirement: Alex is in approved education, which means Child Benefit can continue beyond age 16 (the guidance states 'You'll normally still qualify for Child Benefit if your child is under 20 and they stay in approved education or training').

3. Residential requirement: Alex lives with the claimant, satisfying the responsibility test.

4. Work status: Alex does not work 24 hours or more per week, which is important as working 24+ hours per week while no longer in approved education would disqualify eligibility.

5. Apprenticeship: Alex has not started an apprenticeship in England (which would end entitlement).

6. Benefits: Alex does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit), which would stop Child Benefit.

7. Care/hospital: Alex is not in local authority care, hospital, or residential accommodation, avoiding any 8-12 week time limits on eligibility.

8. Fostering: Alex is not fostered with local council payments, which could affect eligibility.

All conditions for eligibility are satisfied.
